title: They Mock God, Yet They Seem to Win. So Why Does Following Jesus Feel Harder?
paragraphs:
They Mock God, Yet They Seem to Win. So Why Does Following Jesus Feel Harder?
The Dangerous Secret Behind Envying People Who Live in Sin—and the Scandalous Grace That Changes Everything
There is a question many Christians are afraid to admit out loud.
Why do people who ignore God sometimes seem happier than those trying to obey Him?

They laugh.
They travel.
They make money.
They build huge followings.
They appear successful.
They seem free.
Meanwhile, faithful believers quietly carry burdens no one sees.

They pray through sleepless nights.
They fight temptations nobody applauds.
They forgive people who never apologize.
They struggle financially while watching dishonest people prosper.
"Maybe sin isn't as expensive as God says it is."
Most people will never confess that thought.
But God already knows it exists.
That is why He gave us Psalm 73.
Because long before social media made comparison unavoidable...
God already knew His people would struggle with envy.
The Bible never hides the weakness of its heroes.
Instead, it exposes them so grace can heal them.
Psalm 73 begins with one of the most brutally honest admissions in all of Scripture.
The writer is Asaph—a worship leader appointed by King David.
A man who served in God's presence.
Yet even he nearly walked away.
The Hebrew word translated "envious" is קָנָא (qānāʾ).
It carries the idea of burning inside.
A consuming inner fire that asks...
Envy isn't merely wanting what someone else has.
It quietly accuses Heaven of unfairness.
And that makes envy far more dangerous than most people realize.
Asaph watched people openly reject God.
"They have no struggles; their bodies are healthy and strong... Pride is their necklace; they clothe themselves with violence." (Psalm 73:4–6)
Today we scroll through endless feeds.
People proudly celebrate lifestyles God calls destructive.
That question is older than civilization itself.
The serpent never told Eve to stop believing in God.
He simply convinced her God was withholding something good.
The enemy still whispers the same lie.
"Look how much easier their lives seem."
This is why envy is so dangerous.
Even Jesus warned that appearances deceive.
"For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world and forfeit his soul?" (Mark 8:36)
Τί γὰρ ὠφελεῖ ἄνθρωπον κερδῆσαι τὸν κόσμον ὅλον καὶ ζημιωθῆναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ;
The word ψυχή (psychē) means the whole inner life—your soul, your true self, your eternal identity.
The world celebrates what can be seen.
Asaph almost lost sight of eternity.
"Until I entered the sanctuary of God; then I understood their end." (Psalm 73:17)
God did not show Asaph a better earthly life.
He finally saw what temporary success had hidden.
prosperity is only a beautiful road leading toward destruction.
"Wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads to destruction." (Matthew 7:13)
That has never made it right.
Sin often looks rewarding because Satan advertises the beginning...
Hebrews reminds us Moses chose differently.
"He considered the reproach of Christ greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt..." (Hebrews 11:26)
The richest empire in the world.
Because he believed eternity outweighed temporary comfort.
Faith always sees farther than envy can.
The Apostle Paul reached the same conclusion.
"For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory beyond all comparison." (2 Corinthians 4:17)
The greatest answer to envy is not trying harder.
It is looking longer at Christ.
Because Jesus also appeared to lose.
Yet what appeared to be history's greatest scandal became history's greatest victory.
The cross is proof that appearances cannot be trusted.
What looked like failure became redemption.
What looked like shame became glory.
What looked like death became eternal life.
This is why our theme is more than a slogan.
From Scandal to Grace. Because Jesus Rewrites Everything.
The Gospel never promises believers the easiest life.
The Greek phrase ἀνεκλαλήτῳ χαρᾷ (aneklalētō charā) means a joy too wonderful for words.
Perhaps today you have secretly envied someone living apart from God.
Perhaps you have wondered why obedience sometimes feels costly.
God did not reject them for their honesty.
Bring your envy into God's presence before it grows into unbelief.
Tell Him exactly where your heart has wandered.
And His grace is greater than your hidden struggle.
Jesus did not come for people pretending they have perfect faith.
He came for people willing to confess they need Him.
Maybe this article exposed something you have never admitted before.
That is grace inviting you home.
If this spoke to your heart, don't keep it to yourself.
There will be days when scrolling through success, wealth, and worldly pleasure will tempt your heart again. Return to these truths before envy gains a foothold.
One faithful act of obedience is worth more than a lifetime of applauded rebellion.
